standard_prerequisites.name: Existence of a generic point of the intersection of the closure of the point with the fibre, providing the intermediate specialization

standard_prerequisites.use: The intersection of $\overline{\{x'\}}$ with the fibre $f^{-1}(\{s\})$ is nonempty and closed in that fibre, so it has a generic point $x$, giving $x' \leadsto x \leadsto t$.

standard_prerequisites.use: Applied at the intermediate point $x$, where $\mathcal{F}$ is flat over $S$ by the hypothesis, it yields $x \in \text{Ass}_{X/S}(\mathcal{F})$.

core_obligations: Choose a point $t$ of the fibre $X_s$ to which $x'$ specializes (proof line 5187).
Insert the intermediate point $x$, a generic point of an irreducible component of $\overline{\{x'\}} \cap f^{-1}(\{s\})$, so that $x' \leadsto x \leadsto t$ (proof lines 5187-5190).
Apply the hypothesis that $\mathcal{F}$ is flat over $S$ at $x$ and the result on associated points under a flat base change to conclude $x \in \text{Ass}_{X/S}(\mathcal{F})$ (proof lines 5190-5193).
proof_roadmap: Choice of a point in the fibre above the specialization (proof line 5187).
The intermediate point from the fibre intersection (proof lines 5187-5190).
Flatness at the intermediate point and the conclusion (proof lines 5190-5193).
difficulty_reason: The lemma controls the relative associated points under specialization into a fibre: if the sheaf is flat over the base at every point of the fibre and a relative associated point specializes into that fibre, then it specializes to a point which is associated for the fibre itself (statement lines 5174-5184). The proof inserts a generic point of the intersection of the closure with the fibre, where flatness is available by hypothesis, and then applies the standard detection of relative associated points after a flat base change. The insertion of the intermediate point is the substance, so the claim is H2.
